description: Fix the predict endpoint bug, add a predict_single endpoint, and make DATABASE_URL and drift detector optional so the app starts standalone without a PostgreSQL database or drift detector files. All changes are in src/app/main.py only. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 in terms of file conflicts (both touch main.py, but FEAT-001 modifies existing code while FEAT-002 adds new imports and routes), but FEAT-002 depends on FEAT-001's /predict_single endpoint.
steps: Step 1 — Make DATABASE_URL optional: In src/app/main.py, change `DATABASE_URL = os.environ['DATABASE_URL'].replace('postgres://', 'postgresql://')` to `DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL')` followed by `if DATABASE_URL: DATABASE_URL = DATABASE_URL.replace('postgres://', 'postgresql://')`. This is near line 38.

Step 2 — Wrap drift detector load: Wrap the `cd = load_detector(Path('models')/'drift_detector')` call (near line 44) in a try/except block that catches Exception and sets `cd = None` with a print warning. This ensures the app starts even without drift detector files.

Step 3 — Guard GET /drift_data: In the `get_drift_data()` function, add an early check: `if not DATABASE_URL: return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content={"message": "Database not configured"})`. Add `from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse` to imports.

Step 4 — Guard collect_batch: At the top of the `collect_batch()` function, add `if not DATABASE_URL or cd is None: return`. This prevents any DB writes or drift detection when dependencies are unavailable.

Step 5 — Fix POST /predict: Change `model.predict_proba(input_data)[:,0]` to `model.predict_proba(input_data)[:,1]` in the predict() function. This fixes the bug where it returned probability of NOT churning instead of churning. Keep everything else in the endpoint unchanged.

Step 6 — Add POST /predict_single: Add a new endpoint after the existing /predict endpoint. It accepts a bare Customer body (not wrapped in Request): `@app.post('/predict_single') async def predict_single(customer: Customer):`. Build a single-row DataFrame from customer.dict(), call model.predict_proba()[:,1][0] to get churn_probability (float). Return `{'churn_probability': round(churn_prob, 4), 'prediction': 'Churn' if churn_prob >= 0.5 else 'No Churn'}`.

POST /predict returns churn probabilities (class 1) — values should be low for a clearly non-churning customer
POST /predict_single accepts a bare Customer JSON body and returns {churn_probability: float, prediction: 'Churn'|'No Churn'}
POST /predict still works with the original Request body format (backward compatible)
Existing Pydantic models Customer and Request are unchanged

findings: All 6 steps implemented and verified. POST /predict_single is available at /predict_single accepting a bare Customer JSON body. Drift detector failed to load (missing files) but was caught gracefully — cd is None. FEAT-002 can rely on /predict_single returning {churn_probability: float, prediction: string}. The app starts cleanly without DATABASE_URL.
